newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian agrarians walk out in farm funding protest. [CORRECTED 09:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russian agrarians walk out in farm funding protest. [CORRECTED 09:45 GMT]

text.p: Deputies from the Agrarian group in the lower house of Russia's parliament walked out of the chamber on Wednesday, complaining that the government was underfunding the sowing campaign and threatening the harvest.
The 35 deputies said they would only return after Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin explained to the Duma why the farm sector had not yet received any money for this year's sowing campaign.
They said none of the 16 trillion roubles of budget funds allocated for the year as a whole had been paid to the agro-industrial complex.
"Planned spring works in the fields are being undermined, the harvest is being threatened," said Agrarian leader Nikolai Kharitonov.

The State Statistics Committee said on Wednesday Russia's 1997 early spring sowing campaign was running slightly ahead of 1996 levels, with 704,000 hectares sown by April 7, one percent higher than at the same time last year.

Officials are targeting a grain harvest of around 70 million tonnes this year, little changed from last year's poor 69.3 million (Corrects from 63.0 million) tonnes, although independent experts say the harvest could be much lower than that.
